lesson.lesson_summary: Learners meet nouns made from two or more words, written closed (toothbrush), open (post office) or hyphenated (runner-up). They find the main word of a compound, which is usually the last one, and see that changing the order changes the meaning. Plurals of compound nouns are left to 1-2-9.

learning_objectives.description: Recognise a compound noun as one noun made from two or more words.
success_criteria: Find a compound noun in a sentence.

learning_objectives.description: Identify closed, open and hyphenated compound nouns.
success_criteria: Sort compound nouns by how they are written.

learning_objectives.description: Find the main word of a compound noun.
success_criteria: Explain that the last word usually names what the thing is.
Explain how word order changes the meaning.

pages.title: Two Words, One Noun

content.text: Tooth + brush = toothbrush. Some nouns are built by joining two words together.

examples.sentence: I packed my toothbrush and a towel.
examples.explanation: Toothbrush joins tooth and brush to name one thing.

pages.key_takeaway: Two words can join to make one noun.

pages.title: What Is a Compound Noun?

content.text: A compound noun is one noun made from two or more words. Together, the words name one person, place or thing.

examples.explanation: Post + man makes one noun for one person.

examples.sentence: We waited at the bus stop.
examples.explanation: Bus stop is two words, but it names one place.

pages.key_takeaway: A compound noun names one thing with two or more words.

pages.title: Closed Compounds

content.text: Some compound nouns are written as one word, with no space in between.

examples.sentence: The sunflower turned towards the sky.
examples.explanation: Sun + flower is written as one word.
Class + room is written as one word too.

pages.key_takeaway: Closed compounds are written as one word.

pages.title: Open Compounds

content.text: Some compound nouns keep a space between their words, but they still name one thing.

examples.sentence: The post office was crowded today.
examples.explanation: Post office has a space, but it names one place.

examples.sentence: We shared an ice cream after the match.
examples.explanation: Ice cream has a space, but it names one food.

pages.key_takeaway: Open compounds keep a space but name one thing.

pages.title: Hyphenated Compounds

content.text: A few compound nouns join their words with hyphens.

examples.explanation: Brother-in-law joins three words with hyphens to name one person.

examples.sentence: The runner-up won a silver medal.
examples.explanation: Runner-up names the person who came second.

content.title: Tip
content.text: Not sure how a compound is written? Check a dictionary.

pages.key_takeaway: Some compounds use hyphens to join their words.

pages.title: The Last Word Is the Main Word

content.rule_text: In most compound nouns, the last word names the kind of thing. The first word tells us more about it.
content.scope: Most English compound nouns; a few, such as brother-in-law, have their main word first.

examples.sentence: A teacup is a small cup for tea.
examples.explanation: Cup is the main word. Tea tells us what kind of cup it is.

examples.sentence: Our school bus is painted yellow.
examples.explanation: Bus is the main word. School tells us which kind of bus.

pages.key_takeaway: The last word tells you what the thing is.

pages.title: Houseboat or Boathouse?

items.label: Houseboat
items.description: A boat you can live in.
items.example: We stayed on a houseboat in Kerala.

items.label: Boathouse
items.example: The oars are kept in the boathouse.

comparison_points: Houseboat ends in boat, so it is a kind of boat.
Boathouse ends in house, so it is a kind of building.
content.conclusion: Swap the words and you name a different thing.

pages.key_takeaway: Change the order and you change the meaning.

pages.title: Compound Nouns: Recap

items: A compound noun is one noun made from two or more words.
Closed: toothbrush. Open: post office. Hyphenated: runner-up.
The last word usually names what the thing is.
Changing the order changes the meaning.

pages.key_takeaway: Look at the last word to know what it is.

question_bank.prompt: A compound noun is made from two or more words that together name one thing.
question_bank.explanation: The words join to name one person, place or thing, like toothbrush or bus stop.

question_bank.prompt: Identify the compound noun in: 'A butterfly landed on my hand.'
question_bank.target: The noun made from two words.
question_bank.explanation: Butterfly is made from butter and fly, joined to name one insect.

question_bank.prompt: Which compound noun is written as one word?
question_bank.explanation: Football has no space and no hyphen, so it is a closed compound.

question_bank.prompt: Which is an open compound noun?
question_bank.explanation: High school keeps a space between its words, so it is an open compound.

question_bank.prompt: Identify the hyphenated compound noun in: 'My sister-in-law teaches music.'
question_bank.explanation: Sister-in-law joins three words with hyphens to name one person.

question_bank.prompt: In the compound noun 'fire engine', which word is the main word?
question_bank.explanation: A fire engine is a kind of engine, so engine is the main word. Fire tells us what kind.

options.text: A lunch shaped like a box

question_bank.explanation: Box is the main word, so a lunchbox is a kind of box. Lunch tells us what it holds.

question_bank.prompt: Identify the compound noun in: 'The goalkeeper dived to the left.'
question_bank.target: The noun made from two words.
question_bank.explanation: Goalkeeper joins goal and keeper to name one player.

question_bank.prompt: Match each kind of compound with an example.
question_bank.explanation: Keyboard is one word, swimming pool keeps a space and passer-by uses hyphens.

question_bank.prompt: In 'a fruit basket', the main word is basket.
question_bank.explanation: A fruit basket is a kind of basket. Fruit tells us what it holds.

question_bank.prompt: Which compound noun names a kind of shoe?
question_bank.explanation: Snowshoe ends in shoe, so it is a kind of shoe. A shoelace is a lace and a shoebox is a box.

question_bank.prompt: Which sentence contains an open compound noun?

options.text: We met at the railway station.

question_bank.explanation: Railway station keeps a space between its words. Bookshelf and stepmother are closed compounds.
